messages:
jess: saw a wrapped Vault token bundled in a CI artifact that was uploaded to partner S3. scanner flagged it as high severity. s3://partner-uploads/redwood/2026-03-21/build-901/art.tar.gz :eyes:
tony: wrapped or raw?
jess: wrapped. header includes: wrapped:true,kms:key-id=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/ci/cryptoKeys/ci-wrap v=1
ops-bot: automated response -> job 901 aborted, artifact quarantined, runner ci-runner-77 put into quarantine state by ops :warning:
katie: partner-ops, can you confirm removal? we need the object deleted and an archived copy if required for evidence.
partner-ops: removed object and placed archived copy in partner-sec bucket. archive-id: arc-20260321-77. delivering takedown confirmation via email.
sec-oncall: quick checks: 1) find KMS decrypts for key ci-wrap in last 48h, 2) list Vault unwrap ops, 3) hunt for other artifacts with "BEGIN VAULT TOKEN". I see a KMS Decrypt at 2026-03-21T07:42Z by serviceAccount:ci-runner-sa@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com.
tony: good catch. we should create a new key version for ci-wrap immediately and update Vault's wrapping_key. rewrap tokens where feasible. also revoke tokens that might have been unwrapped.
katie: minimal revoke script (run after we enumerate accessors): ```for a in $(vault list -format=json auth/token/accessors | jq -r '.[]'); do vault token lookup -format=json -accessor $a | jq -r '.data.display_name' | grep -E 'ci-runner|build-agent' && vault token revoke -accessor $a || true; done```
jess: ran a quick grep across artifacts from the last 72h, found 3 more hits in builds 894, 899, 901. attaching paths to the incident.
sec-oncall: filing incident INF-2026-356. assigning owners: jess -> evidence & artifact hashes, tony -> KMS key rotation + Vault wrap config, katie -> RBAC policy PR & CI runner policy lockdown, ops-bot -> runner isolation confirmation, partner-ops -> takedown + archive delivery.
partner-ops: we've sent archive manifests and S3 access logs to sec@partner.com; uploaded logs to https://partner-sharing/internal/arc-20260321-77/logs.txt
tony: RBAC notes: CI service account should only have kms.cryptoOperations.wrap/unwrap if absolutely required; prefer a dedicated wrap-only principal for wrapping and forbid token creation. also remove token/issuance capabilities from runners.
katie: drafting PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/compare/ci-minimal-rbac — will include explicit allow list for rewrap service and deny broad token creation. linking runbook to PR.
sec-oncall: we will: A) rotate wrapping key (create new key version), B) rewrap persistent secrets where possible, C) revoke potentially exposed tokens by accessor list, D) sweep artifacts + builds for other leaks, E) harden CI RBAC and update runbook. timeline: immediate actions within 2h.
jess: starting the sweep now (job id sweep-20260321-01). posting results in thread.
ops-bot: runner quarantine confirmed for ci-runner-77 and ci-runner-80.
tony: when revoking, use accessor revocation to avoid race with live tokens. example: `vault token revoke -accessor <accessor>` not revoking by token.
katie: also add per-request audit logging for Vault unwraps and KMS decrypts (extend retention to 90d) — will put this in PR.
sec-oncall: looped in legal/compliance for potential partner disclosure. keep evidence chain intact. do NOT paste raw tokens in this channel.
jess: noted. attaching md5s and object ETags to the incident ticket. will post sweep summary when done. :lock:
sec-oncall: update incident when sweep finishes. great work catching this early, team. :thumbsup:
